messages.author: 6e4b9fac8f01099d
messages.subject: poor mixing of variance components
parts:
I am not completely happy with NUTS(2). I tried stan with a simple variance components model, very similar to the Dyes bugs example (that is also in the stan download file). It is the between group variance component that I expected, with stan, to be better estimated by a better mixing chain for this parameter, compared to the known bad mixing of that parameter in bugs/jags/ordinary gibbs. Maybe I did something wrong, but if any of you have a thought on this, I would very much appreciate sharing.

Here, 3 implementations, one with untransformed between and within variance and inv_gamma priors, and the other with using the precision (1/sig) and gamma priors. The last one is the Dyes example.
http://pastebin.com/fmLgyvTF
Plotting the chain for variance components, specifically the between, shows the poor mixing, that I expected to be better with NUTS/HMC and with its per-parameter step size, compared to gibbs/metropolis.

Thanks
Toby


This is on R 2.15.1, gcc 4.5.1, rstan 1.0.1

parts:
1. That typo is embarrassing. Thanks.

2. I fixed it and the mixing for the between grp and withing grp var is good, when they are both 1 and 1.

3. Now I increase the challange and make the between grp variance small compared to the within grp variance, 0.01 and 1, respectively. Now mixing is again bad and different from what I would expect from the NUTS algorithm that specifically tries to address this issue, especially NUTS 2 with per parameter step size. In all 3 examples. Didn't one of the demonstration papers of even the plain HMC, and also NUTS, have such a difference in magnitude, too, but were successful in estimating them efficiently (n_eff)?
http://pastebin.com/aEVsmiMi

Thanks
T

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] poor mixing of variance components
parts:
Hi Toby,

I'd recommend trying to run the sampler for longer as a first
step—it's possible that the warmup phase wasn't long enough to
accurately estimate the scale of the parameters.

Also, part of the problem may be that the correct answer is fairly
deep in the left tail of the inverse-gamma prior, which is very light.
So the posterior over the between group variance will have a very
light left tail. And NUTS and HMC can sometimes have trouble with
light-tailed distributions (Roberts and Tweedie, 1996). You might have
better luck if you used a less informative prior.

Best,
Matt
